verify: Set its production master key as a runtime secret and verify the image's data path and health endpoint for the chosen release.

title: Existing Dockerfile

title: Multi-stage Dockerfile
approach: Add `deployment.target` to select the runtime stage. [Example](/docs/services/modes/dockerfile)
verify: The selected stage contains the executable and listens on `container.port`.

title: Private packages
approach: Declare `secrets.build` and mount it through BuildKit in a Dockerfile. [Secrets](/docs/secrets/towbar)
verify: The credential is not copied into an image layer or browser bundle.

title: Build server
approach: Set `buildServer` for a source-build Service. [Modes](/docs/platform-deployments)
verify: The builder is registered and has capacity; the runtime server remains the environment target.

title: Static site
approach: Use `deployment.type: static`, `buildCommand`, and `output`. [Example](/docs/services/modes/static)
verify: The output directory exists and the runtime listens on the declared port.

title: Single-page app
approach: In static mode, set `spaFallback: true`. [Example](/docs/services/modes/static)
verify: Direct navigation to a client-side route returns the entry page.

title: Railpack-detected project
approach: Use the pinned `railpack` version and frontend image from its guide. [Example](/docs/services/modes/railpack)
verify: Inspect the detected build and start process; this mode cannot use build secrets.

title: Nixpacks project
approach: Use the pinned `nixpacks` builder and optional `configFile`. [Example](/docs/services/modes/nixpacks)
verify: Its generated image starts correctly; this mode cannot use build secrets.

title: Buildpack project
approach: Pin `packImage` and a reviewed `builder`. [Example](/docs/services/modes/buildpack)
verify: An arbitrary builder digest is rejected; this mode cannot use build secrets.

title: OCI image
approach: Run a reviewed OCI image with an explicit digest. [Image deployment](/docs/services/modes/image)
verify: `latest` is rejected; pin a reviewed tag or digest and verify the image listens on the declared port.

title: HTTP API
approach: Set `container.port` and `health.path`. [Container and health](/docs/services/configuration)
verify: The process listens on the container interface and the path answers without login.

title: Slow startup
approach: Increase `health.timeoutSeconds` only to a measured startup bound. [Container and health](/docs/services/configuration)
verify: A candidate still fails when it never becomes ready.

title: CPU-bound process
approach: Set `container.resources.cpus` and `memory`. [Container and health](/docs/services/configuration)
verify: The target server has capacity for the new and old copies during rollout.

title: Private API
approach: Set `container.network` and omit public `domains`. [Private connectivity](/docs/services/configuration#private-connectivity)
verify: A peer on the same server and network can resolve the alias.

title: PostgreSQL service
approach: Give both workloads `container.network: application`; use the Datastore alias and port in a secret URL. [PostgreSQL](/docs/databases/postgresql)
verify: No credential is committed and the app can connect after database readiness.

title: Redis service
approach: Share a private network and save an authenticated Redis URL as a runtime secret. [Redis](/docs/databases/redis)
verify: The app uses the declared Redis password and the datastore is healthy.

title: Persistent files
approach: Add a named `container.volumes` mount and a `recreate` rollout. [Storage](/docs/services/configuration#persistent-storage)
verify: The runtime user can write the mount and files survive a redeploy.

title: Public HTTPS
approach: Set `domains.primary` and a supported `tls.mode`. [Routing and TLS](/docs/services/routing)
verify: DNS, ingress, and certificate prerequisites are ready before traffic changes.

title: Alternate domain
approach: Add a domain alias according to [routing](/docs/services/routing).
verify: Both hostnames resolve and route to the intended Service.

title: Single-writer data
approach: Use `rollout.type: recreate` with `maintenanceMode: true` and a reason. [Storage](/docs/services/configuration#persistent-storage)
verify: A second process never writes the same volume concurrently.

title: Runtime credential
approach: List its key under `secrets.runtime`, then save the value in **Settings → Secrets**. [Towbar secrets](/docs/secrets/towbar)
verify: Deployment blocks until the selected environment has the value.

title: Build dependency
approach: Declare a build-stage key and use a Dockerfile BuildKit secret mount. [Towbar secrets](/docs/secrets/towbar)
verify: The value does not appear in the committed file or final image.

title: Infisical folder
approach: Set `externalSecrets.integration: infisical`, project, and optional `environmentSlug` or `secretPath`. [External secrets](/docs/secrets/external)
verify: The selected folder returns the required runtime keys.

title: Doppler config
approach: Set `externalSecrets.integration: doppler`, project, and optional config. [External secrets](/docs/secrets/external)
verify: The runtime token can read that config at deployment time.

title: Monorepo auto-deploy
approach: List relevant paths in `autoDeploy.inputs`. [Automation](/docs/services/automation)
verify: Shared packages and lockfiles are included, not only the app directory.

title: Pull-request preview
approach: Enable previews in root `towbar.yml`, then set the Service `preview` block. [Previews](/docs/previews)
verify: Preview secrets are isolated and the preview domain resolves.

title: Daily report
approach: Add a `jobs` entry with an argument-array command and five-field cron. [Jobs](/docs/services/jobs)
verify: It runs from the deployed image and does not overlap itself.

title: Pre-deploy migration
approach: Use a pre-deploy hook and stage-specific secrets. [Deployment hooks](/docs/deployments#deployment-hooks)
verify: The migration is safe to retry and compatible with rollback.

title: Event notifications
approach: Add `notifications` to select workspace-configured destinations. [Notifications](/docs/integrations/notifications)
verify: The destination is enabled and has a tested delivery route.

title: Vulnerability scanning
approach: Set `vulnerabilityScanning` and review the result before release. [Scanning](/docs/vulnerability-scanning)
verify: Findings are assessed for the exact image digest being deployed.

title: Single-service PostgreSQL

verify: The Service uses the declared private network alias on port 5432 and its own secret connection URL.

title: Named PostgreSQL

verify: Set values before first initialization; changing them later does not rename an existing role or database.

title: PostgreSQL tunnel
approach: Add `access.sshTunnel.hostPort` to the Datastore.
verify: Reach the loopback-bound port through SSH; do not publish the database port publicly.

title: PostgreSQL backups

verify: Create and restore-test a representative recovery point.

title: MySQL API
approach: Use `type: mysql`, a private network, and `MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD`.
verify: The app uses port `3306` with an application user, not Towbar's root credential.

title: MySQL schema
approach: Declare `MYSQL_DATABASE`, `MYSQL_USER`, and `MYSQL_PASSWORD` before first deployment.
verify: Check the user and schema actually exist after initialization.

title: MySQL copies
approach: Add a backup destination and retention policy.
verify: The provider credentials are enabled and a restore into a fresh target succeeds.

title: MariaDB CMS
approach: Use `type: mariadb`, private networking, and `MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD`.
verify: The CMS image's client and schema are compatible with this MariaDB major version.

title: MariaDB role

verify: Do not assume changing the saved values rotates an existing role.

title: MariaDB tunnel

verify: An SSH-forwarded client connects; the server firewall does not expose `3306`.

title: MongoDB API
approach: Use `type: mongodb` and the same `container.network` as the API.

title: MongoDB initialization
approach: Declare `MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME` and `MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD`.
verify: Set them before the data volume is initialized.

title: MongoDB user
approach: Create a least-privilege database user after initialization.
verify: The Service uses that user; Towbar's managed root credential stays separate.

title: MongoDB access
approach: Add `access.sshTunnel.hostPort` without public database routing.
verify: The client authenticates to the correct database through SSH.

title: MongoDB recovery
approach: Schedule a provider-backed backup and practice a fresh-target restore.
verify: The archive can be read by an application after restore.

title: ClickHouse analytics
approach: Use `type: clickhouse` on the analytics Service's private network.
verify: The Service reaches the preset's HTTP port `8123`.

title: ClickHouse credentials
approach: Declare `CLICKHOUSE_USER` and `CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD`.
verify: The values are saved in the selected environment before deployment.

title: ClickHouse selection
approach: Optionally declare `CLICKHOUSE_DB` before initial deployment.
verify: The intended database exists and the client is pointed at it.

title: ClickHouse sizing
approach: Set `container.resources` for measured ingest and query load.
verify: The target server has enough CPU, memory, and disk headroom.

title: ClickHouse recovery
approach: Add a supported backup provider and test a fresh-target archive restore.
verify: Query representative data on the restored Datastore.

title: Redis sessions
approach: Use `type: redis`, a private network, and `REDIS_PASSWORD`.
verify: The Service uses an authenticated URL on port `6379`.

title: Redis queue
approach: Give the producer and worker the same private network and secret URL.
verify: Both clients handle reconnection and use the intended database or key prefix.

title: Redis tunnel
approach: Add `access.sshTunnel.hostPort`.
verify: The loopback port is reached only over SSH; no public cache port is needed.

title: Redis recovery
approach: Run a backup and verify a fresh-target RDB restore.
verify: The restored data supports the application and append-only persistence resumes.

title: Dragonfly client
approach: Use `type: dragonfly` and `REDIS_PASSWORD`.
verify: Test the application's actual commands against Dragonfly, not just connection establishment.

title: Dragonfly endpoint
approach: Share `container.network` with the consuming Service.
verify: The Service reaches the Dragonfly alias on port `6379`.

title: Dragonfly recovery
approach: Test a verified snapshot and a same-engine restore.
verify: The restored dataset is readable before traffic moves.

title: KeyDB endpoint
approach: Share a network with the consuming Service and keep the port private.
verify: An authenticated client can use port `6379`.

title: KeyDB recovery
approach: Back up and restore into a fresh KeyDB target.
verify: The target uses the supported KeyDB major version.

title: Manual backup
approach: Configure an enabled storage provider and choose **Back up now**.
verify: The stored copy passes Towbar's restore-readiness check.

title: Daily retention
approach: Add `backup.schedule` with UTC cron and `retention.keepLast`.
verify: The schedule is at least hourly and old copies are eventually removed.

title: AWS S3
approach: Use `backup.integration: aws` with the runtime AWS provider enabled.
verify: The runtime identity can write, read, and delete under the intended location.

approach: Select an enabled `s3` or `r2` provider as appropriate.
verify: Endpoint, bucket, encryption, and credentials match the runtime integration.

title: Google Cloud
approach: Select an enabled `gcs` provider.
verify: The runtime identity can write and read the designated bucket.

approach: Restore a known recovery point into a fresh target.
verify: Query representative data through an application client before promotion.

approach: Override the Datastore's server in another environment.
verify: Save that environment's secrets and confirm its server supports the engine architecture.

title: Password rotation
approach: Change the user inside the database first, then update Towbar's saved value.
verify: Health, application connections, backup, and restore operations all authenticate.

title: Incident investigation
approach: Inspect recovery-point freshness and operation events.
verify: Distinguish a late backup from an unreadable or incompatible one.

verify: The app can query using a non-root application role.

approach: Dockerfile Service + scoped MySQL Datastore; the secret URL uses the Datastore's declared network alias on port 3306. [MySQL](/docs/databases/mysql)
